speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to help me understand your condition, how long have these symptoms been occurring and do you notice any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Ulcerative Colitis).

The history of chronic diarrhea with urgency, mucus, and relief after evacuation is highly suggestive of IBD rather than infectious causes, despite the camping exposure. Given the duration of four months and the absence of fever or severe systemic symptoms, an acute infection is less likely, but stool studies can confirm the absence of pathogens.

REQUEST TEST: Fecal Calprotectin, Stool Culture, Ova and Parasites.
REQUEST IMAGES: Colonoscopy with biopsy if clinically indicated based on test results.
